title: Normalize timezone-aware metering and proration for subminute usage variability
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Some customers with high-frequency (subminute) burst usage are seeing invoice inaccuracies and duplicate/missing invoice lines when usage spans timezone boundaries or DST transitions. Root cause appears to be inconsistent bucketing between the realtime meter, the hourly aggregation job, and the Stripe/NetSuite export windowing.

Symptoms observed:
- Duplicate invoice lines for the same subminute bursts when events arrive late and fall into adjacent hourly buckets.
- Missing proration offsets when a plan change happens within the same hour but in a different local timezone bucket.
- Nightly export diff alerts triggered for affected accounts; manual fixes required for ~0.4% of invoices in the last 90 days.

Investigation notes:
- Reproducer: Account 912-AC (US/PST) on 2026-01-10 had a 12:03:23 burst; metering recorded at customer local time but the hourly aggregators normalized to UTC floor, while the export reconciler used a customer-facing timezone anchor—causing a 1-hour split and a duplicate prorate. Example invoice and raw events attached in the incident ticket.
- Root causes: (1) subminute event timestamps are being rounded inconsistently across services (metering service rounds to nearest second; aggregator floors to minute; export quarantiner floors to hour anchored to account timezone), (2) late-arriving events are merged without idempotent dedupe keys, (3) DST edge-case where local hour disappears/duplicates for affected regions.

Proposed solution:
1) Define a deterministic, account-anchored bucket strategy: all aggregation windows will use the account.billing_timezone as the canonical anchor and apply a consistent rounding policy for subminute events (we will round to 30s and store the rounding delta in the raw event).
2) Add an explicit "window_proof" column to the hourly_aggregate table that contains: window_start_utc, window_start_local, rounding_strategy_version. This will make exports idempotent and auditable.
3) Modify the export reconciler to compute invoice line keys using (account_id, window_start_utc, plan_version, quantity_hash) and to ignore events with event_arrival_time more than 48h late unless quarantined.
4) Implement a backfill/quarantine flow: late events land in a quarantine queue; daily backfill job runs with human-reviewed threshold to avoid automated duplication during plan swaps.
5) Add DST unit tests and property tests for rounding idempotency.

Acceptance criteria:
- No duplicate invoice lines caused by subminute rounding in new exports for a 30-day trial.
- Export diffs for affected customers drop to <0.05% over a 30-day period post-rollout.
- Monitoring: new Grafana panels show "window_mismatch_rate" and "late_event_quarantine_rate" with alert thresholds.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Rounding to 30s may slightly change percent allocation at extreme precision workloads; however, customer-visible cost impact is negligible compared to duplicated invoice risk.
- Quarantine/backfill introduces operational overhead; we constrain auto-ingest only for >48h late arrivals to reduce noise.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): deploy aggregation and window_proof column to staging and to 5 pilot accounts. Run exports in dry-run for 7 days.
- Phase 2: enable reconciler idempotency with 7-day overlapping backfill window for all accounts in region-us.
- Phase 3: global rollout and remove legacy rounding after 30 days, with fallbacks to legacy pipeline for accounts with active disputes.

Follow-ups:
- Create an automation to surface accounts that still rely on second-level precision for contracts to consider per-customer rounding exceptions (follow-up ticket).
- Postmortem checklist item: update runbooks for billing disputes related to timezone-window mismatches.
